newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's net int'l reserves rise to $9.254 billion.
newsitem.headline: Peru's net int'l reserves rise to $9.254 billion.

text.p: Peru's Central Reserve Bank said Friday its net international reserves rose $345 million to $9.254 billion on March 19 from $8.909 billion the previous week.

The bank said in its weekly report that the rise was due mainly to its purchase of $139 million, as well as a $69-million hike in bank deposits and $56 million more in deposits in the state-run Banco de la Nacion.
That was partly offset by sales of $100 million in foreign currency to make payments on Peru's foreign debt, it said.
The central bank also said its foreign exchange position, or total liquidity minus short and long-term debt obligations, was $1.699 billion on March 19, up $28 million from the end of February.
Peru's reserves ended 1996 at $8.540 billion. The government estimates the country's international reserves will rise above $10 billion by mid-1998.
